memories.author: lab
memories.text: INR 2.3 (target 2-3). Serum creatinine 102 µmol/L (reference 62-115). TSH 2.1 mIU/L (reference 0.4-4.0).

memories.author: D05
memories.text: ECG: Sinus rhythm with atrial fibrillation, ventricular rate 78 bpm. No ST-T changes. QRS duration 96 ms.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Atrial fibrillation, COPD and asthma stable.
Patient reports mild dyspnoea on exertion, no nocturnal wheeze. On examination: respiratory rate 18, SpO2 94% on room air, bilateral wheeze end-expiration, regular irregular pulse 78 bpm.
Spirometry: FEV1 1.20 L (55% predicted), FVC 2.10 L (78% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.57; change from previous (none) +0.00 L.
Asthma Control Test score 22 (well controlled).
Inhaler technique: tiotropium HandiHaler inspiratory flow checked 45 L/min, adequate; salbutamol MDI technique checked: correct; budesonide-formoterol DPI technique checked: correct.
Smoking status: former, stopped 2008, pack-years 30.
Plan: Continue apixaban 5 mg BD, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD, warfarin 3 mg OD (INR 2-3). Tiotropium OD, salbutamol MDI SOS, budesonide-formoterol 200/6 BD, montelukast 10 mg HS. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Over the past week I have needed my salbutamol inhaler three times a day due to increased wheeze after climbing stairs. No chest pain or palpitations.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Chest X-ray: Lungs hyperinflated, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation or pleural effusion. Cardiac size within normal limits.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Spirometry: FEV1 1.10 L (50% predicted), FVC 2.00 L (74% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.55; change since last test -0.10 L.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
COPD exacerbation, asthma partially controlled.
Patient notes increased wheeze and salbutamol use three times daily, mild dyspnoea walking 50 m. Exam: respiratory rate 22, SpO2 92% room air, diffuse wheezing, cardiac rhythm irregularly irregular, rate 84 bpm.
Spirometry: FEV1 1.10 L (50% predicted), FVC 2.00 L (74% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.55; change since last test -0.10 L.
Asthma Control Test score 16 (not well controlled).
Inhaler technique: tiotropium HandiHaler flow 38 L/min (suboptimal), counselled to inspire more slowly and deeply; salbutamol MDI technique corrected: coordinate actuation with inhalation; budesonide-formoterol DPI technique checked: correct.
Smoking status: former, stopped 2008, pack-years 30.
Plan: Increase budesonide-formoterol to 200/6 BD (already), add short course prednisolone 40 mg OD for 5 days, continue tiotropium OD, salbutamol MDI SOS, montelukast 10 HS. Continue apixaban 5 mg BD, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD, warfarin 3 mg OD (INR 2-3). Review in 6 weeks.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Refer to Cardiology for atrial fibrillation management and anticoagulation review. Patient 86-year-old male with persistent AF on apixaban and warfarin, borderline renal function. Request opinion on long-term anticoagulation strategy and rate control.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Cardiology outpatient review: Patient reviewed, ECG shows controlled ventricular rate 78 bpm on bisoprolol. Recommend continuing apixaban 5 mg BD, discontinue warfarin due to bleeding risk and borderline renal function. No need for ablation at this time. Follow up in 3 months.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: INR 1.9 (slightly low). Serum creatinine 108 µmol/L (reference 62-115). TSH 2.0 mIU/L (reference 0.4-4.0).

memories.author: D05
memories.text: ECG: Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular rate 80 bpm, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD. No acute ischemic changes.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Atrial fibrillation on apixaban only, COPD stable, asthma well controlled.
Patient denies recent wheeze, uses salbutamol less than twice weekly. No chest pain. Exam: SpO2 95% room air, respiratory rate 16, bilateral mild wheeze, irregularly irregular pulse 78 bpm.
Spirometry: FEV1 1.25 L (57% predicted), FVC 2.15 L (80% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.58; change since last test +0.15 L.
Asthma Control Test score 23 (well controlled).
Inhaler technique: tiotropium HandiHaler flow 48 L/min (adequate), salbutamol MDI technique checked: correct, budesonide-formoterol DPI technique checked: correct.
Smoking status: former, stopped 2008, pack-years 30.
Plan: Continue apixaban 5 mg BD, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD, discontinue warfarin. Continue tiotropium OD, salbutamol MDI SOS, budesonide-formoterol 200/6 BD, montelukast 10 mg HS. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Warfarin stopped. Apixaban 5 mg BD continued. Bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD continued. Tiotropium inhaler OD. Salbutamol inhaler SOS. Budesonide-formoterol 200/6 inhaler BD. Montelukast 10 mg HS.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
COPD and asthma stable, atrial fibrillation on apixaban.
Patient reports no dyspnoea at rest, occasional wheeze on exertion relieved by salbutamol. Exam: SpO2 96% room air, respiratory rate 14, mild expiratory wheeze, irregularly irregular pulse 80 bpm.
Spirometry: FEV1 1.30 L (59% predicted), FVC 2.20 L (81% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.59; change since last test +0.05 L.
Asthma Control Test score 24 (well controlled).
Inhaler technique: tiotropium HandiHaler flow 50 L/min (good), salbutamol MDI technique checked: correct, budesonide-formoterol DPI technique checked: correct.
Smoking status: former, stopped 2008, pack-years 30.
Plan: Continue current medications. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Atrial fibrillation, COPD, asthma all stable.
Patient denies worsening dyspnoea, uses salbutamol less than twice weekly. No adverse effects from apixaban. Exam: SpO2 96% room air, respiratory rate 14, clear lungs to auscultation, irregularly irregular pulse 78 bpm.
Spirometry: FEV1 1.35 L (61% predicted), FVC 2.25 L (83% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.60; change since last test +0.05 L.
Asthma Control Test score 24 (well controlled).
Inhaler technique: tiotropium HandiHaler flow 52 L/min (good), salbutamol MDI technique checked: correct, budesonide-formoterol DPI technique checked: correct.
Smoking status: former, stopped 2008, pack-years 30.
Plan: Continue apixaban 5 mg BD, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD, tiotropium OD, salbutamol MDI SOS, budesonide-formoterol 200/6 BD, montelukast 10 mg HS. Review in 4 months.
